explain.narrative:
## Debugging Java Programs

Debugging is a repeatable process: reproduce, isolate, observe, hypothesize, change one thing and verify. IDE breakpoints pause execution so you can inspect variables and the call stack. Temporary tracing must not expose secrets.

## Applying the concept

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that directly supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failure cases and state assumptions clearly.

## Verification checklist

- Compile with JDK 21.
- Predict the output before running.
- Test normal, boundary and invalid inputs where relevant.
- Check resource cleanup and error handling.
- Prefer explicit types and focused methods.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int price = 12, quantity = 3; System.out.println("trace: price=" + price + ", quantity=" + quantity); System.out.println(price * quantity); } }
examples.explanation: Adds a focused trace before a calculation so the observed inputs can be checked.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int[] values = {4, 8, 12}; int index = 1; System.out.println("index=" + index + ", length=" + values.length); System.out.println(values[index]); } }
examples.explanation: Prints the index and array length before access, making bounds assumptions visible.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int target = 15; int total = 0; for (int n : new int[]{3, 5, 7}) { total += n; System.out.println("after " + n + ": " + total); } System.out.println("target reached=" + (total == target)); } }
examples.explanation: Traces state changes after each loop iteration.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int age = 20; assert age >= 0 : "age must not be negative"; System.out.println("age=" + age); } }
examples.explanation: Demonstrates an assertion for an internal invariant; run with -ea to enable assertions.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String status = "OPEN"; if (!status.equals("OPEN")) { throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected status"); } System.out.println("status verified"); } }
examples.explanation: Uses an explicit condition to verify an assumption before proceeding.

practise.guidedTask: Set a breakpoint before a calculation; predict the values, step through each statement, and record the call stack and variable values.
practise.independentTask: Reproduce an off-by-one bug in an array search. Isolate it, correct it, then add tests for first, last, missing and empty cases.
hints: State the input, output and assumptions before coding.
Use the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior.
Predict the result, compile with JDK 21, then test a boundary or failure case.
practise.challenge: Compare a temporary trace statement with an IDE breakpoint. Remove diagnostic output after verification and rerun the regression tests.
